function.name: read
function.description: Read a file from the workspace. Returns content with line numbers, cat -n style.

file_path.description: Absolute or workspace-relative path to the file to read

offset.description: Line number to start reading from, 1-based

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: write
function.description: Create a new file or overwrite an existing one. Overwriting a file requires having read it first in this session.

file_path.description: Absolute or workspace-relative path to write

content.description: Full content to write to the file

function.name: edit
function.description: Replace an exact string in a file with another. old_string must match exactly once unless replace_all is set. Requires having read the file first in this session.

file_path.description: Absolute or workspace-relative path to the file to edit

old_string.description: Exact text to replace, without any line-number prefix

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match

function.name: bash
function.description: Run a shell command in the workspace. Output is captured and returned once the command exits, unless run_in_background is set, which returns immediately with an id job_output and job_kill can act on.

timeoutMs.description: Maximum wall-clock time for the command, in milliseconds. Omitted, the command gets the harness default, which is short; name a timeout for anything that builds, installs, packages or runs a test suite. A value above the harness ceiling is clamped down to the ceiling rather than rejected, so a larger number buys no more time. The message a timed-out command returns names the limit that actually applied. Work that cannot finish inside the ceiling has to be split into steps, or started with its output redirected to a file that a later call reads.

description.description: A short human-readable description of what the command does

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background instead of waiting for it to exit. The call returns immediately with a job id; read its output so far with job_output, and stop it with job_kill. Use this for a dev server, a watcher, or anything else meant to keep running rather than finish.

workdir.description: Directory to run the command in, absolute or workspace-relative. Defaults to the workspace root. A path outside the workspace is refused, the same as every other path argument.

function.name: job_output
function.description: Read the output a background job (started by bash with run_in_background) has produced since the last time it was read, and whether it is still running.

job_id.description: The id of the background job to read, as returned by the bash call that started it

filter.description: A regular expression. Only output lines matching it are returned; the rest are still consumed and will not be returned by a later call.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes before returning, up to this call's own timeout. A wait that runs out returns the output so far and leaves the job running.

function.name: job_kill
function.description: Stop a background job started by bash with run_in_background. Killing a job that has already finished is a no-op.

job_id.description: The id of the background job to stop, as returned by the bash call that started it

function.name: job_list
function.description: List every background job this session holds: its id, the command it runs, when it started, and whether it is still running or has exited.

function.name: glob
function.description: Find files by path pattern, e.g. **/*.go.

path.description: Directory to search from; defaults to the workspace root

function.name: grep
function.description: Search file contents by regular expression. Defaults to returning matching file paths only.

path.description: File or directory to search; defaults to the workspace root

glob.description: Glob to filter which files are searched, e.g. *.go

type.description: File type to search, using ripgrep's own type names, e.g. js, py, go, rust. More efficient than glob for a standard file type; an unrecognised name is refused.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output. Only for output_mode: content, ignored otherwise. Default true.

-A.description: Lines to show after each match. Only for output_mode: content, ignored otherwise.

-B.description: Lines to show before each match. Only for output_mode: content, ignored otherwise.

-C.description: Lines to show before and after each match; takes precedence over -A and -B. Only for output_mode: content, ignored otherwise.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and a pattern can span multiple lines. Default false.

head_limit.description: Limit the output to its first N lines or entries — files for files_with_matches, lines for content, entries for count. Applied whichever mode is in use, after everything else the call would otherwise return.

function.name: web_fetch
function.description: Fetch a URL and answer a question against its content.

prompt.description: What to extract or answer from the fetched page
